title: Complaint of Stephen P. Engel vs. Evangel Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC found no error in Presbytery’s refusal to decide guilt or innocence without a trial record, but found error in its failure to remand the unresolved charges. It sustained the complaint and sent the matter back for Presbytery to rehear, with the Session ultimately to initiate proper process or formally dismiss the charges.
first_summary: A member challenged Presbytery’s refusal to determine his guilt or innocence and its failure to return charges after his Session suspended him from the sacraments without trial. The SJC sustained the complaint on the remand issue and sent it back for rehearing, while declining to decide guilt or innocence because no trial record existed.
summary: A member challenged Presbytery’s refusal to decide his guilt or innocence and its failure to return charges after his Session suspended him from the sacraments without trial or confession. The SJC sustained the complaint on the remand issue: rescission of the censure did not dispose of pending charges, so Presbytery had to rehear the complaint and require the Session either to institute proper process or dismiss them. It declined to determine guilt without a trial record and rejected the claim that the censure’s prescribed form willfully took the Lord’s name in vain.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The caption identifies SJC Case 2007-04; the opinion records panel concurrence and a 17-member concurring vote (lines 13, 128–130).
evidence_notes.dispute: The complaint asked whether Presbytery erred by declining to determine guilt and by failing to return the matter for proper proceedings (lines 51–57).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC answered no on guilt because no trial record existed, but yes on remand because serious charges remained unresolved despite rescission of the censure (lines 59–65, 107–124).
evidence_notes.qualifications: Presbytery had already corrected its earlier reclassification of the appeal; the SJC also rejected the allegation that use of BCO 36-5’s censure language was willful misuse of the Lord’s name (lines 97–109, 126).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No external decision was incorporated by reference; the opinion independently recounts and evaluates the Session’s and Presbytery’s actions (lines 87–110).

source_limits: The synopsis relies only on the supplied opinion; the underlying record cited as RROC was not provided.
